text: Gajakesari Yoga: Jupiter in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house) from the natal Moon. One of the most celebrated yogas — confers intelligence, fame, wealth, and good reputation. 'Gaja' (elephant's strength) + 'Kesari' (lion's brilliance). Strongest when Moon and Jupiter are unafflicted and in good signs. Fully activated during Jupiter or Moon dashas. Jupiter aspecting the Ascendant or 5th from Moon enhances results. Common in charts of respected scholars and public figures.

Budha-Aditya Yoga: Mercury and Sun conjunct in the same sign. Creates sharp analytical mind, eloquent communication, success in intellectual pursuits, writing, media, and business. Most powerful in Gemini, Virgo, Aries, or Leo. Mercury 10–15° from Sun is ideal; within 6° risks deep combustion limiting Mercury's independent results. Best in Mercury or Sun dashas. In 10th house: exceptional career through intellect and leadership. Among the most common and potent yogas in Jyotisha.

Raja Yoga: lords of kendra houses (1, 4, 7, 10) and trikona houses (1, 5, 9) conjoin, mutually aspect, or exchange signs. Most powerful: 9th + 10th lords combined = Dharmakarmadhipati Yoga. 5th + 10th lords, or 1st + 9th lords conjunct = very strong Raja Yoga. Multiple Raja Yogas in kendra or 10th house = political leaders, CEOs, powerful public figures. Yogas activate most fully during dashas of participating planets when strong by sign and transit.

Dhana Yoga: combinations indicating wealth accumulation. Key formations: (1) Lords of 2nd and 11th conjoin or aspect each other. (2) Lords of 1st, 2nd, 5th, 9th, or 11th form favorable connections. (3) Jupiter in 2nd, 5th, 9th, or 11th. (4) Venus in 2nd with strong 2nd lord. Most powerful: multiple wealth lords converging in 11th. Lakshmi Yoga: Venus in own/exalted sign in kendra or trikona. Dhana Yogas manifest during dashas of the participating planets.

Ruchaka Yoga (Pancha Mahapurusha): Mars in own sign (Aries or Scorpio) or exaltation (Capricorn 28°) AND in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house). Produces: exceptional physical prowess, military valor, athletic excellence, courage under fire, leadership in difficult situations, strong physique and vitality. Native may be a soldier, athlete, surgeon, or executive. Most powerful when Mars occupies the 10th kendra. Activated fully in Mars Mahadasha (7 years).

Bhadra Yoga (Pancha Mahapurusha): Mercury in own sign (Gemini or Virgo) or exaltation (15° Virgo) AND in a kendra. Produces: outstanding intellect, eloquent speech, skill in science and arts, commercial genius, physical grace. Native excels in writing, education, business, computing, or medicine. Mercury exalted at 15° Virgo in 10th kendra = strongest possible Bhadra. Activated in Mercury Mahadasha (17 years). One of the most intellectually distinguished yogas.

Hamsa Yoga (Pancha Mahapurusha): Jupiter in own sign (Sagittarius or Pisces) or exaltation (5° Cancer) AND in a kendra. Produces: divine wisdom, handsome/noble form, charitable nature, spiritual wealth, great respect in society. Native is a wise teacher, judge, or spiritual leader. Jupiter exalted at 5° Cancer in the 1st or 10th is most powerful. Activated in Jupiter Mahadasha (16 years). Among the most auspicious yogas in Vedic astrology.

Malavya Yoga (Pancha Mahapurusha): Venus in own sign (Taurus or Libra) or exaltation (27° Pisces) AND in a kendra. Produces: physical beauty, artistic genius, happy and prosperous marriage, material prosperity, charismatic personality, affinity for luxury. Venus exalted at 27° Pisces in the 4th or 7th = strongest expression. Native succeeds in arts, entertainment, fashion, or luxury. Activated in Venus Mahadasha (20 years), the longest planetary period.

Shasha Yoga (Pancha Mahapurusha): Saturn in own sign (Capricorn or Aquarius) or exaltation (20° Libra) AND in a kendra. Produces: longevity, authority through disciplined effort, mastery in service-related fields, technical expertise, leadership of large organizations. Native excels in law, engineering, government, agriculture, or mining — fields requiring patience and systematic effort. Saturn exalted 20° Libra in 10th = maximum public authority. Activated in Saturn Mahadasha (19 years).

Kemadruma Yoga: Moon has no planets (excluding Sun, Rahu, Ketu) in the 2nd or 12th houses from it. Indicates emotional instability, loneliness, and financial struggles. More pronounced in Moon Mahadasha. Cancelled (Kemadruma Bhanga) when: (1) Moon in a kendra from Ascendant, (2) planet in a kendra from Moon, (3) Moon aspected by a benefic, (4) Moon conjunct another planet. When cancelled, results paradoxically become very strong — native overcomes hardship to achieve significantly.

Neecha Bhanga Raja Yoga: debilitated planet's weakness cancelled, producing results often stronger than exaltation. Cancelled when: (1) Sign lord of the debilitation sign is in kendra from Moon or Ascendant. (2) Planet exalted in that same sign is in kendra. (3) Debilitated planet itself is in kendra. (4) Debilitated planet is aspected by its sign lord. Classic examples: Saturn in Aries with Mars in kendra; Jupiter in Capricorn with Saturn in kendra.

Viparita Raja Yoga: lords of the 6th, 8th, or 12th placed in each other's houses or conjoined, away from kendra/trikona lords. Converts misfortune into fortune — native rises through others' downfall or sudden reversals. Three types: Harsha (6th lord in 6th or 8th), Sarala (8th lord in 6th or 12th), Vimala (12th lord in 6th or 8th). Native wins over enemies, survives crises, benefits from hidden sources. Strongest during dashas of these planetary lords.

Chandra-Mangala Yoga: Moon and Mars conjunct in the same house. Creates emotional drive, passion, and financial ambition. In good houses (1, 5, 9, 10, 11) unafflicted: success in business, sports, real estate, military, entrepreneurship. In difficult houses (6, 8, 12) or with malefics: impulsiveness, conflicts with women, marital discord. Energies peak during Moon-Mars or Mars-Moon antardasha. Gives strong desire for financial independence and courageous action on instinct.

Adhi Yoga: natural benefics (Jupiter, Venus, Mercury) placed in the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses from natal Moon (all three houses occupied). Creates natural leaders, ministers, commanders — prosperous, influential, and long-lived. More benefics = more powerful: all three houses occupied by strong benefics = head of state or equivalent stature. Results manifest fully during dashas of participating benefic planets. One of the few yogas requiring all three benefics simultaneously.

Kalasarpa Yoga: all seven classical planets (Sun through Saturn) fall between Rahu and Ketu on one side of the chart. Considered challenging — recurring karmic obstacles, delays, struggles tied to past-life patterns. Not found in classical texts (relatively modern concept). Partially cancelled if even one planet falls outside the Rahu-Ketu axis. When Rahu and Ketu occupy strong houses (6th, 11th, 3rd), Kalasarpa can produce remarkable success after significant hardship and karmic clearing.

Sunapha Yoga: planet (except Sun) in 2nd from Moon — wealth, self-made success. Anapha Yoga: planet in 12th from Moon — freedom, spiritual inclination, health. Durudhura Yoga: planets in both 2nd and 12th from Moon — worldly success plus spiritual wisdom. Vasumati Yoga: all benefics in upachaya houses (3, 6, 10, 11) from Moon — immense wealth. These yogas shape how Moon's planetary relationships affect fortune; named according to the Sanskrit terms for flanking planet positions.

Solar flanking yogas formed by planets around the Sun. Vasi Yoga: planet (except Moon) in 12th from Sun — eloquent, generous, persevering native. Vosi Yoga: planet in 2nd from Sun — learned, wealthy, skilled in arts and crafts. Ubhayachari Yoga: planets in both 2nd and 12th from Sun — highly fortunate combination of wisdom and eloquence. These yogas strengthen the Sun and give it additional planetary support, enhancing solar significations of authority, vitality, and creative power.
